Real Estate.summary: Ridgewood, New Jersey band whose hazy, reverb-soaked debut about suburban boredom became foundational to the 2010s jangle revival.

Red House Painters.summary: San Francisco band led by Mark Kozelek whose slow, unhurried, extended-form confessional songs helped define sadcore alongside Low and Codeine.

Red PK.summary: Chicago songwriter, also the pedal steel player in Tobacco City, making hushed, banjo-and-pedal-steel folk-country under his own name.

Red Red Meat.summary: Chicago band on Sub Pop playing woozy, blues-damaged roots-rock with slurred, understated vocals that directly seeded Califone.

Red Simpson.summary: Bakersfield-scene songwriter who carved out the trucker-song niche within hard country using the same treble-forward Telecaster sound as his peers.

Remember Sports.summary: Philadelphia band whose scrappy basement pop-punk grew into tighter, anthemic power pop within the city's DIY network.

Renata Zeiguer.summary: Brooklyn songwriter making dreamworld folk-pop that mixes hushed vocals, vintage guitar tones and bossa nova influence.

Renée Reed.summary: Lafayette, Louisiana songwriter whose dreamy, lo-fi debut mixes Cajun-inflected folk melody with woozy, four-track-style production.

Rhett Miller.summary: Old 97's frontman whose solo debut leans further into power pop than his main band, made with Jon Brion's polish.

Richard Buckner.summary: Lubbock-rooted songwriter whose lyrically dense, literary records grew from insurgent-country debut into noisier, atmospheric, indie-adjacent territory.
Richard Buckner.related: Lloyd Maines; Giant Sand; Marc Ribot; Tortoise

Richard Thompson.summary: Former Fairport Convention guitarist whose first solo album mixed accordion and Northumbrian pipes into dry, story-driven English folk-rock.

Richard and Linda Thompson.summary: Post-Fairport Convention duo whose decade-long partnership produced increasingly electric, then devotional, then harder-rocking folk-rock albums.

Richmond Fontaine.summary: Portland band led by Willy Vlautin, playing lean, pedal-steel country-rock built around Raymond Carver-indebted short-story songwriting about drifters and gamblers.

Rick Danko.summary: The Band's bassist and singer, whose only solo album is a gentler, more overtly romantic singer-songwriter record than his main band's catalog.

Rick Nelson & the Stone Canyon Band.summary: Former teen idol's country-rock reinvention, trading pop-idol sound for pedal-steel-driven songwriting alongside the Byrds and Burritos scene.
Rick Nelson & the Stone Canyon Band.related: Randy Meisner; Poco; the Flying Burrito Brothers

Riddy Arman.summary: Montana ranch hand and musician whose spare, lonesome country-folk debut about rural isolation sounds genuinely lived-in.

Ride.summary: Oxford band whose shoegaze debut balances guitar squall with clearer, more anthemic songwriting than My Bloody Valentine.

Robber Robber.summary: Burlington, Vermont quartet whose thick, distorted, start-stop guitar rock hits harder and more explosively than the band's earlier work.

Robbie Basho.summary: Berkeley guitarist whose Takoma-label debut pushed fingerstyle playing toward Native American imagery and Indian classical raga, distinct from Fahey's blues roots.
Robbie Basho.related: John Fahey; Sandy Bull; Jack Rose; William Tyler; Marisa Anderson

Robbie Fulks.summary: Chicago songwriter whose classic honky-tonk shuffle and pedal steel carry sharp, funny-sad wit descended from Prine and Tom T. Hall.
Robbie Fulks.related: Hank Williams; Buck Owens; John Prine; Tom T. Hall

Robert Earl Keen.summary: Houston-and-Austin storyteller whose rowdy, narrative Texas songwriting grew directly out of a college friendship with Lyle Lovett and the Guy Clark tradition.
Robert Earl Keen.related: Lyle Lovett; Nanci Griffith; Guy Clark; Townes Van Zandt

Robert Forster.summary: Brisbane songwriter whose post-Go-Betweens solo debut, made in Berlin, traded string-pop sheen for drier, more theatrical literary narratives.
Robert Forster.related: the Go-Betweens; Grant McLennan; Einstürzende Neubauten

Robert Hunter.summary: The Grateful Dead's non-performing lyricist stepping out as a singer-songwriter, working the same rustic, image-dense American vernacular he supplied to the band.
Robert Hunter.related: the Grateful Dead; Jerry Garcia; Bob Weir; New Riders of the Purple Sage
